correctness.rationale: The exact singular-value recurrence is a_i^+=|a_i-m| for positive a_i with m=sum(a_i)/4 and sticky zero entries. On r<4 nonzero support the signed linear chamber map I-ss^T/4 has eigenvalues 1 and 1-r/4>0, excluding finite annihilation; a direct squared-norm descent shows asymptotic convergence. A strict two-above/two-below step gives u,v,w,z, then two repeated-pair values, then equal magnitudes and zero, except lower-dimensional degeneracies. A one-versus-three chamber maps normalized ratios y_i to 1-2y_i, forcing finite exit except exactly equal one-third triplet; all exceptional ties are a countable union of proper hyperplanes on piecewise-linear branches, giving Lebesgue-a.e. finite termination. Along (3,1+t,1,1-t), the iteration and dyadic hit condition yield exact T=N(t)+5 and rank-deficient nontermination at dyadic resonances. Independent Fraction recurrence confirms T(1/5)=6, T(1/9)=7, T(1/100)=10, and nontermination at t=1/16,1/32. Those finite checks are not the almost-everywhere proof.

value.rationale: The distinction between convergence and literal finite termination is mathematically substantive for a nonsmooth matrix optimizer. The explicit four-mode piecewise-linear dynamics and exceptional dyadic resonances give a sharp dynamical classification and show why uniform stopping-time bounds fail.

final_claim: For nuclear-scaled polar descent on a 4x4 isotropic quadratic at step 1/4, almost every full rank matrix terminates at zero in finitely many steps while every nonzero rank deficient matrix never terminates. For singular values (3,1+t,1,1-t), 0<t<1/4, exact stopping T=N(t)+5 off dyadic inverse powers; inverse powers never terminate.
